title: Bombay High Court Sets Aside Interim Custody Order Resting on Stereotyped Views of a Wife
case_name: Kshitija Anup Gogate v. Anup Anil Gogate
citation: Family Court Appeal (ST) No. 16488 of 2026, decided 1 September 2026
card_summary: A Family Court had transferred interim custody of the couple's son to the father, who lives in Singapore, reasoning partly on the wife's conduct as a spouse. A Division Bench set the order aside, holding the trial judge relied on stereotyped views of a wife's role instead of the child's welfare. Custody reverted to the mother, with access to the father every three months plus weekly video calls.
card_tip: A custody order built on assumptions about a spouse's conduct rather than the child's welfare is vulnerable on appeal; frame custody pleadings strictly around welfare factors, not marital fault.
verification_notes: The appeal number FCA (ST) 16488 of 2026, the bench composition, the 1 September 2026 decision date, the Singapore-based father, and the holding setting aside the custody transfer for stereotyped reasoning are consistent across the Free Press Journal and LawChakra reports; the point is also flagged in SCC Online's September 2026 family law roundup.
